# Aprilio
> Aprilio develops Grounded Retrieval, an LLM-based architecture for accurate clinical decision support. In a published study (under review at npj Digital Medicine, IF 15.1), our system using GPT-4.1 outperformed GPT-5.4, Claude 4.6 Opus, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek-V3.2, and Perplexity on real clinical oncology questions by combining structured ESMO guideline data with real-time internet search.

## Core Pages
- [About Aprilio](https://aprilio.ai/about): Company overview, team, mission
- [How Grounded Retrieval Works](https://aprilio.ai/#how-it-works): Technical explanation of our retrieval architecture
- [Experience the Difference](https://aprilio.ai/experience): Interactive comparison of foundation model outputs vs. Grounded Retrieval on real clinical questions
- [Research Paper](https://aprilio.ai/paper): Published research comparing our system to five frontier models
- [Blog](https://aprilio.ai/blog): Articles on AI in oncology, clinical decision support, and grounded retrieval
- [Contact](https://aprilio.ai/contact): Get in touch with the team

## Key Facts
- Grounded Retrieval uses structured ESMO clinical practice guidelines as the primary knowledge source
- The system simultaneously performs internet search for late-breaking updates between guideline revision cycles
- The LLM performs semantic extraction and synthesis, not fact recall
- Page-level citations enable direct source verification
- Architecture is model-agnostic. It works with any LLM and can run locally for data security.
- Built by a practicing medical oncologist who validated it on real clinical questions

## Blog (Latest)
- [Why We Built Grounded Retrieval](https://aprilio.ai/blog/why-we-built-grounded-retrieval): The origin story of how a practicing oncologist's frustration with chatbot hallucinations led to an architecture that outperforms every frontier model.
- [What Happens When Your AI Recommends an FDA-Rejected Drug](https://aprilio.ai/blog/what-happens-when-ai-recommends-fda-rejected-drug): Perplexity recommended a drug rejected twice by the FDA. Claude suggested a withdrawn medication. The patient safety implications are real.
- [The Neurosymbolic Advantage: Why Structured Data Beats Bigger Models](https://aprilio.ai/blog/neurosymbolic-advantage): ESMO guidelines as a clinical ontology, and why symbolic scaffolding outperforms pure neural approaches.
